subject.title: [Feature]: cron jobs.d/ directory support (one file per job, for NixOS/GitOps declarative setups)

question: Should OpenClaw add a declarative per-job cron file workflow, and should that workflow reconcile into SQLite or become a steady-state directory-backed runtime store?
rationale: Current code and docs make SQLite the canonical cron store, while this request adds new storage/config behavior with migration, identity, deletion, and path-safety implications that automation should not choose unilaterally.

options.title: Reconcile Into SQLite
options.body: Add a documented deterministic import/export or reconcile path that validates per-job JSON and writes canonical SQLite rows without making file polling the runtime store.

options.title: Runtime Directory Store
options.body: Add a new directory-backed cron store mode with explicit migration, symlink, path-safety, stable filename, and upgrade semantics.

options.title: Decline Core Storage Mode
options.body: Keep the supported path as CLI/Gateway API plus external user-side scripts or a ClawHub plugin for file reconciliation.

recommendation.title: Reconcile Into SQLite
recommendation.body: Add a documented deterministic import/export or reconcile path that validates per-job JSON and writes canonical SQLite rows without making file polling the runtime store.

likelyOwner.reason: The current cron persistence and SQLite storage boundary most directly traces through steipete's merged cron store work.
